windows.definition: scheduled-arrival cohorts, half-open, relative to actual event time t_f (monotonic time immediately before os.kill, or the corresponding instant without a signal)

plan.latency_definition: gated latency = actual task start to terminal outcome; prediction percentiles over all attempted terminal requests of the cohort; explanation success latency over successful requests; scheduled-to-terminal also reported, not gated; linear-interpolation percentiles (committed function)

prediction_gates: full and per-window p95 within allowed increase

instrumentation.service: scratch wrapper around the committed app and committed Dispatcher: passive method wrappers (submit, send, start, terminate, _fail_worker, _finish, _step_starting), one 100 ms sampler thread (dispatcher state, cgroup CPU/throttle/memory/OOM, per-process state, CPU ticks at 10 ms resolution, threads, fds, RSS), one 100 ms event-loop lag task, two probe routes inside the isolated network
instrumentation.injector: separate process (docker exec) inside the service PID namespace; armed at the target; the wrapper sends one local datagram right after a successful explain dispatch; the injector validates the target (spawn_main command line, not resource_tracker, child of the API process, not PID 1, the only worker) and sends one signal. It shares the service cgroup.
instrumentation.generator: shim around the unmodified committed generator: exports t_start and collects distinct non-success response bodies
instrumentation.identical_across_runs: same files and settings in all six runs. Differences: DF0 sends no signal; after a signal the injector polls /proc every 10 ms until the old PID disappears (about 0.02 s DF1, about 0.77 s DF2); DF0 does not poll

overhead.not_measured: wrapper, injector and probe-route cost; no uninstrumented A/B run was made (six-run limit). Instrumented results are not claimed equivalent to unmodified execution. The sampler adds one parent thread; the probe retains job objects in process memory only.

clock.domain: CLOCK_MONOTONIC of the one Docker VM kernel, used by generator, service, probe and injector
clock.verification: same boot_id; container time namespaces have different IDs but zero monotonic and boottime offsets; three cross-container bracketed reads satisfied A < B < C
clock.uncertainty: timestamps share a domain; event time is read immediately before os.kill (call returned within 0.4 ms). Raw ledger times are rounded to 1 us. Process state and CPU observations are limited by the 100 ms sampling and 10 ms tick resolution.

smoke_test.configuration: P2 rates, 2 s warm-up + 6 s measurement, arming and notification without a signal

analysis_revisions: After the primary runs: the first analyzer version assigned cohorts from ledger scheduled times rounded to 1 us, which could move the arrival at exactly +10 s into warm-up and produced false reconciliation failures (2,999 instead of 3,000). Membership now uses the nominal schedule t_start + k/rate; identities, cohort labels and counts reconcile exactly. No gate or threshold changed.

After the primary runs: milestone rule 11 (generator scheduling invalidity makes affected, unattributable service-performance conclusions NOT VERIFIED) was implemented. It was not spelled out in the frozen plan. It changed three DF2-r1 latency gates: two numeric PASS and one numeric FAIL (prediction post-window p95) are NOT VERIFIED, each keeping observed_numeric_result.

anomaly_detail.DF2_r1_second_timeout: request 1468, generation 2, dispatched at t_start+39.777 s with a 250 ms budget; exec_timeout at about t_start+40.04 s with an empty queue. 26 arrivals scheduled 39.79-39.99 s were issued late (39.83-40.07 s). In the same interval a sampler interval stretched to 164 ms, parent event-loop lag reached 23.8 ms, and in one 92 ms interval the worker was in state R with zero added CPU ticks. No cgroup throttling period was added.
anomaly_detail.DF2_r1_other_disturbances: around t_start+26.0-27.0 and +28.5-29.5 s, generator scheduling lag (15-29 ms) and prediction latency (up to 148 ms) rose together with no restart and no throttling period
anomaly_detail.DF1_r1_late_saturation: about 15.8-20.0 s after injection (t_start+35.8-40 s), long after readiness: queue at 8, explanation latency up to 412 ms, 23 explanation_overloaded rejections, no restart or throttling; approximate worker CPU per success rose from about 16 ms (DF0) to about 28 ms in t_start+34-40 s

overall_rationale: DF0 (2/2), DF1-r2 and DF2-r2 meet all gates. DF1-r1 fails one gate (23 explanation_overloaded rejections outside the recovery interval). DF2-r1 fails six gates (generator scheduling validity for both streams; an uninjected second execution timeout and replacement; consequent classification, error and post-drain gates) and has three NOT VERIFIED latency gates.

historical_comparison.controlled_results: In four injected replacements, each recovery interval added 2 CFS throttled periods (435-709 ms throttled time); DF0 measurement windows added none. No injected replacement reproduced a multi-second prediction stall or any missed arrival; prediction latency maxima in fault event windows were 85-87 ms (event cohort).
historical_comparison.reading: The historical throttle signature (2 periods, 689.5 ms) is of the same order as that of a controlled replacement, so it is consistent with a replacement having occurred and does not by itself explain a 2 s stall. DF1-r1 (overload rejections without a restart) and DF2-r1 (an uninjected execution timeout coinciding with generator lag) resemble parts of the historical sequence at much smaller scale. This is not a reproduction of P2_r3 and does not establish its initiating cause.

confirmed_findings: All 24,000 scheduled predictions in the six runs succeeded with no missed arrival and no contract or association violation, including through the four injected replacements. DF2-r1's uninjected replacement began as arrivals ended, so it gives almost no evidence about predictions during that replacement.
In every valid fault cohort, prediction p95 stayed within the predeclared allowance and event-window p99 was at most 66 ms. DF2-r1 post and full latency conclusions are NOT VERIFIED.

The actual recovery interval is not covered by a predeclared p95 gate. Prediction p95 over it was 45.8 ms (DF1-r1), 12.9 ms (DF2-r1), 14.5 ms (DF2-r2) and 14.4 ms (DF1-r2), against about 7 ms without a fault.
SIGKILL of the confirmed active worker was classified active_eof; the active request returned 503 explanation_unavailable. Replacement was ready after 2.38 s and 2.40 s.

SIGSTOP of the confirmed active worker was classified exec_timeout at about 250 ms; the active request returned 504. SIGTERM did not end the stopped process and the committed policy's SIGKILL did, about 0.77 s after injection, with no emergency cleanup. Replacement was ready after 3.17 s and 3.08 s.

In every replacement the old PID was absent when the next worker started. No request ID was dispatched twice or finished under another generation, no future was left unresolved, capacity stayed within 1/8/9, and observed error bodies were fixed sanitized envelopes.

Peak memory was about 40% of the limit, with no OOM. After 15 s idle plus one health call, fds and threads met the predeclared bounds; elevated parent thread counts after drain (up to 28) returned to 12. All shutdowns were clean.

At 40 explanations/s the single worker normally used about 0.65 core (about 16 ms CPU per explanation). When CPU time per success rose to about 28 ms (DF1-r1), the bounded queue filled and requests were rejected.
unresolved_hypotheses: Cause of the DF2-r1 uninjected timeout and of its 26-30 s disturbances: simultaneous effects in the generator and service containers without cgroup throttling are consistent with a host or VM level stall; no host telemetry was collected, so this is correlation only.

Cause of the higher per-explanation CPU time in DF1-r1: reduced effective CPU speed (host contention, SMT sharing, frequency) is plausible and untested. A delayed effect of the earlier replacement is neither shown nor excluded. In the same t_start+34-40 s window DF1-r2 and DF2-r2 showed no rise (about 16 ms); DF2-r1 was not computed because its worker was replaced inside that window.

Replacement start-up (process, model and Captum initialization) coinciding with CFS throttling is a plausible mechanism for the brief prediction latency rise; temporal coincidence does not establish causality, and the phases within start-up were not separated.
Initiating cause of historical P2 repetition 3: unresolved.
limitations: One host, two repetitions per condition; incidence of the uninjected anomalies cannot be estimated.
Instrumented execution; overhead only partly measured and no uninstrumented control.
No host-level CPU, disk or scheduler telemetry.
DF2-r1 post-recovery success for generation 3 was not observed: the single post-drain check arrived while it was starting (503). Generation 2 had served successful, contract-valid explanations.
SIGSTOP models an unresponsive worker; it does not model a CPU-bound or slow worker.
Latency under client deadline semantics of schema 2 is not comparable one-to-one with schema 1 history.
Raw ledgers, traces and logs are kept only in a session scratch directory and may not survive cleanup.
recommended_next_step: Under a separately approved, diagnostic-only milestone, repeat the no-fault P2 profile several times with unprivileged host and VM CPU telemetry plus per-explanation child CPU and wall time, to establish how often generator/service stalls and explanation CPU-cost inflation occur without any fault. No production correction is justified by this evidence.

gate_accounting.note: Same 182 gates in all three. v0 is preserved as a historical outcome of a defective analyzer, not as a reviewed result. Overall result is FAIL under all three. All six primary runs are retained; the smoke test is retained and is not a repetition. No run was added, replaced or discarded.

analyzer_boundary_correction.defect: v0 tested half-open window membership using the ledger's scheduled time, which the committed generator rounds to 6 decimals. In five runs the value for arrivals lying exactly on a boundary rounded 0.077-0.384 us below the unrounded boundary.

analyzer_boundary_correction.correction: v1 uses the nominal schedule t_start + k/rate with the half-open test written as a-1e-9 <= nominal < b-1e-9.
analyzer_boundary_correction.uses_original_unrounded_timestamps: Partly. t_start was persisted unrounded and nominal times repeat the generator's own expression. Unrounded per-request values were never persisted; every ledger value is within 0.5 us of its nominal time.
analyzer_boundary_correction.independent_check: Warm-up, full and whole-run membership recomputed from the integer arrival index alone (no timestamps) equals v1 for every request. For pre, event, post and recovery, strict half-open comparison of nominal times (no 1 ns tolerance) equals v1 for every request.

analyzer_boundary_correction.correction_to_earlier_wording: analysis_revisions says 'No gate or threshold changed'. Definitions, windows and thresholds did not change, but 10 gate statuses changed from FAIL to PASS, run results changed from 1 PASS / 5 FAIL to 4 PASS / 2 FAIL, and success counts, success-rate denominators and some percentiles changed. It also described only the +10 s arrival; the +0 s arrivals were affected too.
analyzer_boundary_correction.reproducibility: v0 was not saved as a file (it was patched in place). Its text and both patches were extracted verbatim from the session command transcript. Applying both patches to it reproduces the on-disk final analyzer byte for byte; rerunning it on the preserved records reproduces the output saved at the time byte for byte (apart from that file's leading plan-hash line). v1 and v2 reruns match their recorded gate lines; the v2 JSON equals the original final JSON. The original v0 and v1 JSON files had been overwritten; the archived copies are regenerated.

DF2_r1_event_window_review.conclusions: prediction event p95 10.037 ms (limit 6.619+5 = 11.619 ms) and event p99 40.384 ms (limit 100 ms)
DF2_r1_event_window_review.reviewed_status: PASS retained: SUPPORTED, window-scoped and qualified
support: per-request lag is complete for the window: predict n=500 p99 2.926 max 3.713 ms; explain n=200 p99 2.652 max 3.229 ms; none above 10 ms
the whole event cohort had completed by t_f+5.018 s; the first later arrival issued more than 10 ms late was scheduled at t_f+6.464 s
the pre window is likewise free of arrivals more than 10 ms late
qualifications: generator CPU and event-loop lag were recorded only as run aggregates (maximum 127 ms, not time-located). A stall of that size would be expected to delay several arrivals, which the window's maximum lag does not show; this is an inference, not window telemetry
retaining a window conclusion from a run that failed run-level validity is a post-hoc attribution judgment
it says nothing about the full-run or post-event conclusions and does not turn the failed generator gates into a PASS

confirmed_findings: Prediction correctness and availability were observed in all six runs.
Both intentional recovery mechanisms (active-worker kill; execution-timeout) operated successfully, two of two each.
Prediction latency showed measurable interference over actual recovery intervals (p95 12.9-45.8 ms against about 7 ms without a fault). No actual-recovery p95 gate was predeclared and none is added.
DF1-r1 had unexpected late-run overload (23 rejections).
DF2-r1 had an unexpected additional execution timeout and failed generator scheduling validity.
The original P2 repetition 3 incident was not reproduced.
remaining_uncertainty: Host or VM disturbance is a hypothesis.
Why CPU time per explanation rose is unknown.
Replacement start-up interference is a plausible mechanism, not an established root cause.
The initiating cause of P2 repetition 3 is unknown.
